extracted.intended_audience: NIH fellowship peer reviewers and scientific review officers (SROs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer reviewers assessing NIH fellowship (Fellowship) applications under the revised review criteria effective Jan 25, 2025; focuses reviewer attention and expectations for critiques and meeting tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate's Preparedness and Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three revised core review criteria. Reviewers should assess the fellowship candidate's preparedness and potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised criteria are meant to better focus reviewer attention on the fellowship candidate's preparedness and potential. Academic grades will no longer be a component of fellowship applications; instead, the candidate, sponsor and referees may provide a variety of information for the review panel to determine the candidate’s preparedness and potential. See 'Reviewer Guidance on Evaluating NIH Fellowship Applications' (PDF) and 'Fellowship Reviewer Training Slides' for additional guidance on evaluating this element and writing effective critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Training Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three revised core review criteria. Reviewers should evaluate the quality and appropriateness of the proposed research training plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Research Training Plan is a key assessment area under the revised framework; reviewers should judge whether the proposed plan will provide rigorous, appropriate research training that advances the candidate's development. Detailed assessment guidance and examples are provided in the consolidated reviewer documents (PDF guidance and training slides).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three revised core review criteria. Reviewers should evaluate the sponsor's and institution's commitment to the candidate's training and success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The revised criteria emphasize the commitment to the candidate without undue consideration of sponsor and institutional reputation. Reviewers should focus on concrete evidence of mentoring, resources, and support for the candidate rather than relying on perceived prestige of the sponsor or institution. See reviewer guidance documents for examples of appropriate evidence to consider when assessing commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize broad range of candidates and training contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle underlying the revisions: clarify and simplify language so a broad range of candidates and research training contexts can be recognized as meritorious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should apply criteria in ways that do not unfairly favor particular training models, institutions, or background profiles. The intent is to allow diverse career paths and training contexts to be judged meritorious; refer to the reviewer guidance documents for direction on inclusive, context-sensitive evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form: information use (academic grades removed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural change: the PHS Fellowship Supplemental Form has been updated and academic grades are no longer a component of fellowship applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because academic grades are no longer part of the application, reviewers should not use grades as evidence of preparedness. Instead, reviewers should consider the alternative information provided by the candidate, sponsor, and referees on the updated supplemental form when judging preparedness and potential. The supplemental form aligns application content with the revised review criteria; reviewers should consult it when writing critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Other review criteria that supplement the core criteria (unchanged by the revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes that no changes have been made to the Additional Review Criteria. Reviewers should continue to apply any established additional criteria (as applicable) in accordance with existing NIH guidance and the consolidated reviewer documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Review Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Other review considerations that inform assessment beyond the three core criteria (unchanged by the revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No changes have been made to the Additional Review Considerations; reviewers should continue to follow existing guidance about these considerations as provided in NIH policy and reviewer materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer meeting and critique tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational expectations: reviewers are provided consolidated documents that describe assessment of specific review elements and review meeting-associated tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resources available to reviewers include 'Reviewer Guidance on Evaluating NIH Fellowship Applications' (PDF) and 'Fellowship Reviewer Training Slides' (PDF) intended for SRO-led orientation sessions. Reviewers should use these materials to guide scoring, writing effective critiques, and participating in panel discussions consistent with the revised framework.
